items.note: S2.1 says a fixed linear network exchanges two banks and restores auxiliary values, and S2.2 names the three-element-subset construction, but neither gives the copy/gather/scatter/side-injection schedule, the y_S+x_S update or the (X,Y)->(-Y,X) map.

S2.1 says that with an invertible frame per gate the intermediate frames cancel and only an endpoint operator remains, which is the substance of eq:common-frame-identity, but it gives no edge operator D_vD_u^{-1}, no formula D_out S D_in^{-1}, and not the reason (a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate).
No step mentions subspace labels, orthogonal residuals, the loss L=Ich or the budget Wm-2N+2L, so the source of s<Wm is left unexplained.
S2.2 gives the bit network with W wires and edge-difference rank total s<Wm, quoting the proposition. It omits the endpoint condition M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m and the value s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
S3's method says to use the complex network with phase frames, but no step gives the frames C_U, the one-kernel-per-residual-vector factorization, s_c, or the C^{tensor m} endpoint.
The plan states s<Wm and a power m^tau with tau<1, quoting line 1326, but gives neither the explicit tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} nor the deficits eta, and it states the saving only for the bit network.
S1 lists linear-time scans, digit-pair permutations and controlled shifts. It omits the cyclic row split into W streams and the condition that the offset is prepared in b^{O(1)} time.

S2.4 names the lower-triangular factorization correctly but says the shear is done in linear time per matrix. The paper's point is that it costs exactly a=rank interchanges, which are recursive calls, plus O(V). It also writes H+D for H+AD.

S2's method (network with rank saving, edges by shears, recurse) and S2.3 (s calls at size f on volume V/W, power m^tau) follow the paper's route. Missing are the row field divisible by W^k, the three-shear conversion of H<-H+D into the interchange, and the O(1)-per-node recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with its fixed-tape schedule.
S2.5 states the O(Vu^tau) interchange for arbitrary width, matching the lemma. There is no account of the padding and base-m splitting.
S3's method mentions phase frames and frame changes by packed selected-bit additions, but gives no conjugation by P_M, no s_c children of size e/m and no H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S C^{tensor D} S.

S3.1 states the XOR at positions rho+iK correctly, but calls it one packed pass. The paper uses eight whole-chunk rotations plus a repair of a bad set, at cost O(V(L^tau+1)), and the plan gives no cost.
S3's method ends with 'and recurse', and no step gives F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the row field or the exponent conditions.

S3 and S3.2 state H_0 on one bit of up to d chunks in O(Vd^{lambda'}), exact Gaussian dyadics and one truncation. They omit K=floor(d^c), the parameter regime and the error bound sqrt2 2^{-p}. The route (phase frames, packed additions, recurse) is the paper's, but the recurrence, the child count s_c and the guard-width argument are missing.

The plan gives powers of y as roots acting as signed shifts, a layout so that the layers apply, and a stored frequency order. It omits F^+F^-=t^{-1}I, the counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, the error and the cost formula.

S4.2 says ring products come exactly from integer multiplication by signed packing with the known O(n log n) multiplier, but it says one integer product where the paper makes four. It also gives no B_0=2^{4p} and no cost O(rp log(rp)).

S4.3 gives two forward transforms, a pointwise product and the opposite transform, with the retained order in S4.1. The error is only 'bounded', and the normalization (f*g)/(rM) and the cost are missing.

S5 and S5.1 say that transforms of coprime lengths go to power-of-two tensor transforms with both permutations kept in the formula. There is no identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA and no theta condition, and S5.1 mislabels which length is the power of two.

The plan states that the source permutation cancels across two forward transforms, a product and the opposite transform, and that Bluestein turns the middle factor into a convolution. Neither formula and no chirp a_j is given.
S6.5 refers to a fixed rational choice of exponents including kappa=2^{-182}, but gives none of the other values, the sizes b,p,d,K,T or the choice of primes s_i.
S6.2 states a CRT reindexing onto cyclic axes of distinct prime lengths that preserves convolution. It gives neither Phi nor its triangular digit form.
S6.3 says a phase twist makes the last axis negacyclic modulo y^r+1, without zeta=e^{pi i/r} or the identity M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g).

S6 and its children give the chain (radix digits, CRT axes, power-of-two axes, ring, rounding, carries). They omit the source transform F=2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A=RF_s, its conjugate and the scaling by S and 2^{2b+4}S.

S6.4 states that errors stay below 1/2, so rounding and carries give the exact product. The paper's <1/2 is for the final scaled coefficient error (eq:final-error), not for every transform, and no bound, p=6b or gamma<=b/4 is given.
S6.5 states that each cost divided by V=Tp is a power of p below one, giving O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). It lists no cost terms and does not give the minimal margin g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa.
No step says that the bound refutes an n lg n lower bound in this model.

errors.says: The address shear (H,D)->(H+D,D) with a rational matrix is done in linear time per fixed matrix via lower-triangular factorization.
errors.paper: The shear (H,D)->(H+AD,D) costs exactly a=rank(A) interchanges of b-digit fields plus O(V); the triangular parts are linear, but each one of Pi is an interchange, and these are the recursive calls whose count is the rank.

errors.says: Selected bits of grouped address chunks can be XORed in one packed pass.
errors.paper: Eight whole-chunk cyclic rotations give the result away from a small bad set, which is then repaired. The cost is O(V(L^tau+1)+MA^3+delta_bad MA(R+A)), not a single pass.

errors.says: Ring products are obtained from one integer product by signed packing.
errors.paper: Real and imaginary numerators are evaluated at B_0=2^{4p}, and four integer products A_aA_c, A_bA_e, A_aA_e, A_bA_c are made.

errors.says: Gaussian resampling expresses a Fourier transform of a prime-power-free length t through a power-of-two transform.
errors.paper: The transform of length s (coprime to t, s<t; the s_i are distinct odd primes) is expressed through the transform of the larger length t, which is the power of two.

errors.says: All transforms keep the coefficient error below 1/2.
errors.paper: Transform errors are O(ell 2^{-p}) and chain to E_w<28 2^gamma T^2 L; the bound below 1/2 is for the final coefficient error after the scalings.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route at the top level: interchange, then the simultaneous layer, synthetic transforms, resampling with retained permutations, CRT and chirp, recovery and accounting. Each piece is mostly asserted rather than derived. It thins out badly at the source of the saving: the label and residual budget (L<N/2) is absent, the complex phase interface, phase-frame recursion and layer recurrence are only named, and S2.4 misstates the shear as linear time, which hides the step where rank becomes the number of recursive calls. The final accounting gives no cost terms or margins, and the explicit parameters are not stated.
